thread:
Olivia: Quick postmortem follow-up from the cache-thrash incident. We identified a recurring pattern where large concurrent prefix loads + autoscaler churn results in KV cache evictions and a traffic spike to cold model variants. Need to update the runbook with clearer triage steps, exact commands, and an explicit escalation path.

Olivia: Proposal: 1) Add a 'verify cache health' step with a clear command and expected output. 2) Add immediate mitigations (force warm variants, scale-up policy override). 3) Escalation: oncall -> eng-sre -> platform oncall if scaling fails.

Dave: I can take ownership of the runbook edits. Will PR with changes and a small test scenario. Assign to me: runbook update + smoke test. :thumbsup:

Maria: I'll update the playbook checklist and add a short pre-shift run that exercises the KV cache verification. Will add the explicit thresholds (eviction rate > 5% over 10m triggers runbook).

Sree: Suggest adding a small diagnostic script and a one-line command people can paste. Also add a fallback step to pin model variant via the routing policy. We should include exact metric names and sample Grafana query.

Chris: Where should the runbook live? Is it under infra/runbooks/cache-eviction or incidents/runbooks?

Olivia: infra/runbooks/cache-eviction.md — link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-eviction (post the PR there).

Incident Bot: New postmortem asset uploaded: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/cache-thrash-206412 (sha: a1b2c3).

Yuki: Here’s a concise command we used during triage to check KV eviction counts and node health, put this in the runbook as-is:

Yuki: ```
# check recent KV evictions per node (last 10m)
kubectl -n inference exec -it svc/kv-metrics -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_eviction_total | tail -n 50"
# expected: evictions_per_min < 0.05 * cache_size (per node)
```

Maria: Good — will paste that into the triage section under "Verify cache health" and add the Grafana URL and a sample query.

Dave: For immediate mitigation steps I'll add this sequence (to run while paging platform):

Dave: ```
# 1) pin warm model variant (fast fallback)
redwoodctl routes update --route default --model model-v2-warm --force
# 2) temporarily raise reserved capacity
redwoodctl capacity set --pool inference-prod --gpus 10
# 3) disable autoscaler for 5m
kubectl -n infra annotate hpa inference --overwrite autoscales=false
```

Sree: Add note: these actions are high-impact, require oncall + eng-sre approval unless incident severity is P0. Include exact rollback commands.

Olivia: Action items/owners and timelines:
- Dave: runbook PR with mitigation steps + rollback commands — due in 48h.
- Maria: playbook checklist + metric thresholds + Grafana query — due EOD 3 business days.
- Yuki: add diagnostic command block + small test harness (unit test for script) — due 72h.
- Sree: coordinate canary test scenario and review the PRs — due 96h.

Chris: Can we also add a short section with "What to expect" when you pin variants (latency bump, cost impact)? That helps oncall make informed decisions.

Olivia: Yes — include expected latency delta and estimated cost delta per hour. Maria will add numbers to playbook.

Maria: One more: add an explicit escalation phone tree for the platform oncall if scale-up command fails (include paging tags and the fallback email alias).

Dave: Will draft the PR now. Tagging reviewers: @Maria, @Sree, @Yuki.

Sree: I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up review 72h from now to smoke-test the runbook steps against a dev cluster. Calendar invite to follow.

Olivia: Thanks all. Please add your PRs and link them here so we can close the postmortem follow-ups in the tracker. :eyes:
